solution_ideas.headline: Find Equivalent Green Coffee Substitutes Fast
solution_ideas.short_description: Match disappearing spot lots to available green-coffee substitutes using cup-profile adjacency, trade flows, forecasts, and price signals.
solution_ideas.description: A roaster enters the origin, lot characteristics, blend role, target flavor profile, annual volume, and acceptable price range for a spot coffee that has disappeared or become uneconomic. SpotGapBlend combines the lot brief with ICO price indicators, USDA production forecasts, UN Comtrade import flows, and a curated origin-and-cup-profile taxonomy to rank substitute origins and comparable lots. Each result explains why it matches, shows supply and price signals, identifies likely importer or sourcing routes, and highlights compromises such as acidity, body, processing, or lead time. The roaster can compare candidates, save a replacement plan, and export a sourcing brief for importers or purchasing staff. As new trade and crop data arrives, saved gaps are re-ranked and users are alerted when a stronger substitute becomes commercially plausible.

solution_ideas.headline: Printable lot reconciliation sheet for café production stock
solution_ideas.short_description: Generate a one-page roast lot form that records actual yield, café drawdown, and remaining stock for each specific coffee lot.
solution_ideas.description: A roaster opens the single-page tool, enters the lot name, green weight in, roast date, and optionally selects bean density and roast level to pre-fill an expected-yield estimate. The tool generates a printable PDF with dedicated fields for the roasting profile, actual roasted weight out, café production drawdown, and remaining stock. After roasting, the user writes the scale reading and café drawdown onto the sheet, then subtracts drawdown from actual roasted weight to reconcile the specific lot. The completed sheet can be filed beside production records, preserving lot identity without requiring an inventory platform, integrations, or online access.

solution_ideas.headline: Translate Roast Curves Into Expected Cup Behavior
solution_ideas.short_description: Train shared-roastery operators to connect roast curves, development choices, and green-coffee lineage to sensory outcomes before cupping.
solution_ideas.description: A trainee starts by selecting a coffee’s variety or genetic group from the World Coffee Research catalog, then uploads an Artisan or Cropster export or enters batch milestones manually: charge temperature, turning point, first crack, development time, end temperature, roast color, and roast loss. The tool compares those values with the selected lineage’s documented agronomic and cup descriptors, then presents a bounded expectation—not a guaranteed prediction—for acidity, body, sweetness, clarity, and likely roast-related risks at the observed development level. After cupping, the trainee records actual scores and notes; the tool places expected versus observed results side by side and explains which production action to try next, such as shortening development, changing energy earlier, or testing a different endpoint. Trainers can turn anonymized roast-and-cup pairs into reusable lessons for the shared roastery, while each recommendation remains traceable to the logged roast variables, lineage context, and prior observations. The MVP focuses on teaching the translation loop rather than replacing cupping or attempting fully automated profile control.
solution_ideas.value_proposition: Roast-to-Cup Translator turns a trainee’s roast curve and green-coffee lineage into explainable sensory expectations and concrete next-batch adjustments.

solution_ideas.headline: Consolidate Café Orders Into Fewer Roast Batches
solution_ideas.short_description: Upload café orders and batch capacity to combine same-coffee orders into fuller runs, cutting repetitive small-batch roasting time.
solution_ideas.description: The roaster uploads a weekly café or wholesale order CSV, maps each ordered SKU to a roast recipe, and enters the usable batch capacity for each machine. The tool groups orders that share the same recipe, combines quantities across cafés, and calculates a batch plan that fills runs without exceeding capacity or violating simple separation rules. The user sees the original order lines beside a consolidated schedule showing batch number, recipe, total roast weight, contributing cafés, and the portion to allocate back to each order. If exact capacity prevents a perfect fit, the optimizer shows unavoidable leftover capacity and compares alternative schedules by batch count and estimated roasting time. The roaster exports a production checklist and allocation sheet for the roast day; no forecasting, purchasing, or inventory planning is included.
solution_ideas.value_proposition: Convert fragmented café orders into the fewest practical same-recipe roast batches, so an undersized roaster spends less time repeating partial runs.
